consequences: During x's A-root tenure, x's B-depth is FROZEN (no B-growth possible).
Tenure contains only x-DELETEs (no-ops: x at root, zero rotations) plus the ending access; S_A and pools-needs are constant over tenure except the ending access.
An a=1 KEEP (x at A-root) has need = max(D-1,0) with D = B-depth frozen since tenure start; if tenure started with a KEEP, D=0 and need=0 unconditionally.
computational_check: root-dislodging confirmed: 0 bystander-at-root survivals across 2000 hostile histories (any other access with rotations dislodges A-root)
proof_T1: Splay loop rotates iff node has parent; 0 A-rotations iff accessed key already at A-root. Rotation-free accesses are exactly root accesses.
proof_T2: Splay brings accessed key z to root; single root exists; x != z leaves root. Hence any other access with >=1 A-rotation ends x's A-root tenure.
proof_T3: B-depth(x) changes only via B-rotations, which occur only at KEEPs. During A-root tenure the only legal accesses are x-accesses (others would rotate and dislodge x by T2) and rotation-free accesses (root = x, i.e. x-accesses). x-DELETE: A unchanged (root, no rotations), B untouched. Hence B-depth(x) constant over tenure.
